claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, there are specific rules that apply. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over if they're under 20 and stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or doing an apprenticeship?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college anymore. But he has started an apprenticeship - he's training up in Aberdeen, Scotland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify what type of apprenticeship Alex has started, as this is important for determining eligibility.

**Is Alex's apprenticeship in England, or is it a different type of apprenticeship in Scotland?**

The reason I ask is that the rules specifically state that Child Benefit stops if a child starts an apprenticeship in England. I need to understand whether his Scottish apprenticeship would be treated differently.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's a Scottish apprenticeship - he's doing his training in Aberdeen, which is in Scotland, not England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question to help determine Alex's eligibility:

**How many hours per week is Alex working as part of his apprenticeship?**

This is important because Child Benefit stops if a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's working full-time as part of the apprenticeship - it's definitely more than 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also confirm a couple more details to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK, and are Alex's living arrangements still that he lives with you at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's the situation:

**The key issue** is that Alex has started a Scottish apprenticeship in Aberdeen and is working more than 24 hours per week. The rules I have access to specifically state that Child Benefit stops if a child:
- Starts an **apprenticeship in England**, OR
- Starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training

However, the rules only specifically mention **apprenticeships in England**. They don't provide clear guidance on how apprenticeships in Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland are treated. Scottish apprenticeships may be treated differently and could potentially count as "approved training" (which would maintain eligibility), or they may be treated the same way as English apprenticeships (which would end eligibility).

**What you should do:**

I'd strongly recommend that you **contact the Child Benefit Office directly** to clarify how Scottish apprenticeships are treated under the Child Benefit rules. They will be able to give you a definitive answer about Alex's eligibility.

You can contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office by phone or through their online services to get specific guidance for your situation.
